Q: How to address kubernetes load balancer profile cyclic dependency A:

Outbound IP address does not have to be in managed resource group. It can be anywhere, but AKS has to have right to edit them (to assign them to load balancer).

It means, you have to use UserAssignedIdentity when creating cluster. You first create IP address and some identity with rights to assign that IP address (and possibly any other resources like DNS zones if you are using), then create AKS cluster with link to given IP in load balancer profile block and given identity in identity block.

Inbound IP address can be created separately. Yes, you can use one of outbound IP addresses as inbound, but you can create inbound address AFTER cluster creation. This inbound IP address HAS to be in managed resource group. You first create cluster, then create IP in managed resource group and then you create Kubernetes LoadBalancer referring to this IP.

Be aware, that using outbound IPs for inbound traffic can cause problems with outbound NAT ports when using application, who does "heavy" background jobs causing requests to external internet services.

Q: Why do nested flexbox items shrink differently? A:

The Firefox DevTools "Layout" tab explains the computations. Here's an example screenshot for one of the elements:

Let's read the first (blue) line of the "Layout" tab for each element, starting with the inner elements:

  • .a has width: 700px; and thus a "Base Width" of 700px
  • .b has some text, in my default font the "Content Size" is 160px
  • .inner contains the two things above, summing up to a "Content Size" of 860px
  • .c has flex-basis: 700px; and thus a "Base Size" [sic!] of 700px

Now let's traverse back from the outside to the inside:

  • .outer:

    • .outer contains .inner and .c, whose sizes have a ratio of 860:700, see above. Both have a flex-shrink value of 1 (see the second (pink) line of the "Layout" tab). So the numbers of pixels by which they shrink should have a ratio of (1·860):(1·700).
    • And their shrunk sizes should sum up to 500px because .outer has width: 500px; (near the bottom of the "Layout" tab, under "Box Model", it says 500).

    To achieve these two goals, .inner shrinks by 584.37px (see the second (pink) line of the "Layout" tab) to a "Final Size" (see the third (black) line) of 275.63px, and .c shrinks by 475.63px. I get a slightly different last digit with 860-500/(860+700)*860 no matter how I round, but whatever.

  • .inner's "Final Size" is 275.63px (see above). It contains .a and .b.

    • .b has flex-shrink: 1 (second (pink) line) but this is overridden by min-width: fit-content;, so it has the same "Minimum Size" (third (purple) line of the "Layout" tab) as its "Content Size" of 160px.
    • .a has flex-shrink: 1 (second (pink) line). For .b with 160px and .a to sum up to the 275.63px of their parent, .a shrinks to 115.63px.

Verdict

The final size ratio gets computed from numbers such as 700px and 160px even though some of them get shrunk and don't appear anywhere in the final layout whereas others remain unchanged. No use cases come to mind where such a size ratio is meaningful design-wise.

This is probably just a fast hack (for breaking a circular dependency between the absolute size and the size ratio?) rather than the best solution to a system of equations or optimization problem that formalizes the designer's typical and explicitly implemented intentions.

Q: Sorting Organization's Repos by "newest" or "creation date" A:

The way I've found to do this (Answer is AI assisted) in the CLI is:
gh repo list <ORD_GOES_HERE> --json name,createdAt --jq 'sort_by(.createdAt) | reverse | .[] | [.name, .createdAt] | @tsv'

I'm pretty sure this can't be done in the website.

Q: Why clangd on windows cannot find standard header files? A:

MinGW users should install MinGW Clangd from the same source as their compiler. MSYS2, for example, packages it in mingw-...-clang-tools-extra. This should just work out of the box.

It's not strictly necessary, but it saves the effort of manually configuring the stock Clangd that defaults to MSVC-compatible mode.

If you don't want that, I'd recommend adding --target=x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --sysroot=C:/msys64/ucrt64 to clangd flags (replace ucrt64 to match your compiler flavor in MSYS2).

Those can be added e.g. in the .clangd config file, that you can create in the root directory of the project:

CompileFlags:
    Add:
        - --target=x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
        - --sysroot=C:/msys64/ucrt64

Q: Google Apps Script PUT API call A:

The issue with the API was that the documentation did not mention what was required in the payload.

In the payload, slot parameter was necessary for the API request, even though it was called slotId in the documentation.
